# DKR-024: Containers keep seccomp and AppArmor, and public ones set no-new-privileges

- **Group:** Docker
- **Severity when it fails:** moderate
- **Root:** the full result needs `sudo`. Without root this check may report `unknown`; it never reports a pass it could not verify.

## Why it matters

seccomp=unconfined and apparmor=unconfined remove the default filters that block most kernel escape techniques. no-new-privileges stops setuid binaries inside a container from gaining privileges, which closes a common escalation step for a container reachable from outside.

## Verify by hand

```sh
docker inspect --format '{{.Name}} {{.HostConfig.SecurityOpt}}' $(docker ps -aq)
```

## How to fix it

Remove the unconfined options; add security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"] to public containers, or "no-new-privileges": true in daemon.json for all new containers.

## What a fix can break

Images that rely on setuid binaries (sudo, ping in old images) at run time fail with no-new-privileges.
